thread:
maria: Customer Polaris is seeing steady 429s from their Dedicated pool since ~09:20 UTC. They report <30 rps and still hit throttles. Can someone pick up?
ethan: I can triage. Any quick repro or headers?
maria: Pasting trimmed curl + response headers they sent: 
```bash
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer POLARIS_KEY' 
  -d '{"inputs":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 02 Jul 2024 09:21:08 GMT
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1718005260
X-Redwood-Pool: reserved-prod-42
Content-Type: application/json
```
maria: They also attached service logs which show our quota check returned "0 available units" even though their plan should allow burst.
jessica: @ethan can you check the quota translation for reserved-prod-42? Might be denom mismatch (tokens vs requests).
ethan: Looking now. I see the tenant's plan flags show denom=\"tokens\" but the active ratekey bound to that pool is using denom=\"requests\". That would zero out the computed available units when we apply per-tenant overlays.
kevin: Wait — wasn't there a recent feature-flag rollout that silences legacy per-tenant overrides in the quota service? Could be related.
ethan: Good call. I grep audit logs: featureflag.quota_shim=true rolled at 2024-07-02T08:55:12Z across the quietpool rollout group. For tenants with legacy tags the shim returns 0 to opt them into pooled throttling.
liam: Polaris shouldn't be opted in; they have an enterprise reserved contract. This is a misclassification.
ethan: Repro steps I ran locally with their tenant id: 
```py
# simulate quota calc
plan = {"denom": "tokens", "burst": 1000}
active = {"denom": "requests", "rate": 120}
# mismatch => effective available = floor(burst * 0) -> 0
```
nora: Quick mitigation: can we toggle the feature flag off for that rollout group or patch quota service to prefer plan.denom when overlays conflict?
jessica: I can rollback the FF for the quietpool group. Oncall approval?
ethan: Rolling back the FF will restore previous logic; but we should also patch translation to fall back instead of returning zero. I'll open a hotfix PR after rollback.
jessica: autoscale-bot: rollback scheduled by jessica at 09:45 UTC for featureflag.quota_shim on quietpool rollout group.
autoscale-bot: Feature flag rollback initiated. Expected impact window ~2m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maria: I told Polaris we have a mitigation in progress and asked for sample request ids. They sent two ids: req_3a7 and req_3b1.
ethan: I verified logs for req_3a7 — quota service returned {"available_units":0, "reason":"denom_conflict"}. After rollback should return normal computed units.
kevin: CS follow-up note: Polaris billing/contract shows reserved capacity active since June 1. Need to add a postmortem step: ensure rollout groups exclude enterprise reserved customers.
liam: Affects: throttling + perceived downtime for their features. They want ETA for full fix.
ethan: ETA: rollback completes now, monitor for 5m, then hotfix PR (code + unit tests) by EOD and deploy tomorrow morning.
maria: Polaris confirmed 429s stopped at 09:47 UTC, one-off 503 spike, then normal. I'll keep watch and update ticket. :thumbsup:
kevin: I'll draft a customer note explaining root cause (feature-flag-induced denom override) and corrective actions.
nora: Add automated test to ensure denom translation never returns zero on conflict. I'll own the test.
jessica: Closing loop: rollback complete at 09:47:05 UTC. Reopen if we see recurrence.
liam: Thanks everyone. Good catch. :raised_hands:
